text: There's no glass in the windows, just uneven wooden shutters that kinda close if you kick them hard
enough. So the light comes in, the cold comes in, and the flies come in too. By night, the same gaps
let out the heat you spent all day trying to trap. You don't sleep on a mattress. You sleep on straw
stuffed into a cloth bag. Lice live in it. Fleas live in it. And at this point, you've simply accepted
them as roommates who don't pay rent. Every morning when you stand up, your back feels like you fell
asleep on a pile of gardening tools. You hear movement around you. Because yes, you're not
alone here. Your whole family sleeps in this one room. Everyone. Parents, siblings, children.
And even that one uncle who showed up two years ago, just for a few days, and somehow never left.
